description: Connection interrupted measures commands, not time: shown when the usercmd made 127 commands ago is newer than the last one the server acknowledged (nextSnap->ps.commandTime). One command per client frame makes the warning window 127 frames: about 1 s at 125 FPS, 254 ms at 500, 127 ms at 1000, so high frame rates show it on healthy connections. While the player is not simulating (kill cam, final kill cam) commandTime stops advancing and the window drains even faster.
evidence: CG_DrawDisconnect: CL_GetUserCmd(CL_GetCurrentCmdNumber() - 0x7F); shown if nextSnap->ps.commandTime < cmd.serverTime <= cg.time. CL_CreateNewCommands (004EF7A0): cmdNumber++ into a 128-entry ring (& 0x7F). Store build: CG_DrawDisconnect 1400DA680, CL_CreateNewCommands 1401954D0 (match.py). To confirm in reconstruction: CL_SendCmd (004EC0A0) creates one command per frame, and whether the wrapped ring also costs real command redundancy in CL_WritePacket (004FCB30). Players report it clears when capped at 120 FPS.

description: The game changes Windows microphone settings: Voice_Init sets the record level of every wave-in mixer line to winvoice_mic_reclevel (default 0xFFFF, i.e. 100%) and their mute state to winvoice_mic_mute, and Voice_Playback re-applies the level whenever the dvar changes. Mixer_RestoreWaveInRecordLevels puts them back only on a clean shutdown, so a crash or forced exit leaves the system microphone at 100%. A game has no business changing system device settings; scale the captured samples in the game instead (winvoice_mic_scaler already exists).
evidence: Voice_Init (0079EBD0): Mixer_SetWaveInRecordLevels(Dvar_GetInt(winvoice_mic_reclevel)), Mixer_SetWaveInMuteStates(winvoice_mic_mute). Mixer_SetWaveInRecordLevels: mixerGetLineControlsA(MIXERCONTROL_CONTROLTYPE_VOLUME 0x50030001) then mixerSetControlDetails. Store build imports the same WINMM mixer functions; Voice_Init matched at 14049E3B0.

description: Removes a key with strcpy(start, s) where the two overlap (the rest of the string copied down over the key). Undefined behaviour that works because VC100 expands strcpy into a forward byte copy; Info_RemoveKey_Big (0078ECD0) does the same.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078EC8D: an inline byte loop from s down to start. src/universal/q_shared.cpp reproduces it with tools/recon/include/string.h's forward-copy strcpy.

description: Off by one: the append is refused only when strlen(newi) + strlen(s) > MAX_INFO_STRING (1024), so the string can grow to 1024 characters plus its terminator, one byte past a MAX_INFO_STRING buffer. Info_SetValueForKey_Big (0078F1E0) has the same check against BIG_INFO_STRING. Quake III refuses at >=.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078F140: CMP EDX,0x400; JBE (append). Reachable from the network wherever a caller's string or value comes from a client or server (userinfo); the callers aren't reviewed yet.

description: Stack overflow: a big info string may be up to BIG_INFO_STRING (20480) characters, but each key is copied into an 8192-byte stack buffer with no length check, so a key longer than 8191 characters overwrites the stack. (The value is only skipped: the original's value copy was compiled out.)
evidence: Disassembly at 0078ED31: the key loop writes into [EBP-0x2004] (pkey) until a backslash, with no bound; the only length check is on the whole string (0078ECFD: CMP EAX,0x5000). Whether a caller passes network data isn't reviewed yet.

description: Not the inverse of GetLeanFraction (2f - f*f): any fraction below 1 is first lowered by 0.8, so 0.9 maps to 0.0513 where the inverse is 0.684, and everything up to 0.8 maps to 0.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078FD3E: SUBSS by 0.8 (0x00B95868) when fFrac < 1, then 1 - sqrt(1 - fFrac). Callers (lean prediction) not checked: may be deliberate.

description: Copies the path through a 64-byte buffer before appending the extension, silently cutting any path of 64 characters or more; an empty path reads path[-1].
evidence: Disassembly at 00790308: I_strncpyz(oldPath, path, 0x40) then Com_sprintf(path, maxSize, "%s%s", oldPath, extension). tests/differential/test_q_shared.py covers a 70-character path.

description: A destsize of 0 writes dest[-1]; a negative one copies all of src and writes before dest. Only an assert guards it, and retail builds compile asserts out.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078E080: dest[destsize - 1] = 0 unconditionally; the copy loop counts destsize down to 0.

description: A '?' facing the end of the string steps past the terminator and keeps matching whatever follows in memory.
evidence: Disassembly at 0078E3F8: '?' matches any character, including the terminator, without stopping.
